Today's international headlines:
- Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.
- Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy: The share price dropped wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the value of Nvidia.
- Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say: Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are all sending delegation to the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
- Trump says more US attacks on Iran 'highly unlikely': The president says the US is keeping "status quo" with Iran but remains “locked and loaded” should the situation change.
- Epstein associate who still runs model agency 'put me in danger' says abuse survivor: A woman says an agency boss sent her to photoshoots at the sex offender's Florida beach home.
- Australia considers criminal penalties for rogue AI in wake of OpenAI hack: AI safety regulator will also be created after a rogue OpenAI agent hacked government websites.
- Republican congressman to force impeachment vote on Defence Secretary Hegseth: The effort will likely fail, but Representative Thomas Massie wants to push Trump to fire Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process next year.
- France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking: Tons of chilled and frozen food was spoiled last month as fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets heated up.
- Qantas to outsource 850 local jobs with most roles moving to India: The Australian airline said the move was aimed at modernising its IT systems and noted the impact of AI.
- Russia's leading independent newspaper closes after eviction: The outlet has been evicted from its offices of three decades and says it's been blocked from receiving donations.
- Turkey steel factory blast kills at least 17 people: Eyewitnesses say the explosion shook the ground, with one believing an earthquake had hit near the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga.
- Judge denies motion to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's murder case: The ruling means the case can move forward, possibly with reduced charges in a new trial.
